baseline_sources.source_title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
baseline_sources.evidence_status_basis: OpenAI directly states the chronology, scale of the multi-agent effort, its denial of specific user-data access, and its caveat that de-identified usage-derived data may have helped improve its models.

limitations: The publication is OpenAI's own account of disputed conduct and does not independently verify its internal data-access or training claims.
No internal access logs, model-training lineage or complete prompt corpus were reviewed.

baseline_sources.interpretive_reliance: Primary first-party source for OpenAI's chronology, compute scale and post-publication investigation. The 10 September update materially narrows the specific hypothesis that Buckmaster's recent Codex prompts influenced the proof, including through training. It does not substitute for independently auditable internal telemetry across every possible tool, retrieval or data pathway.
baseline_sources.relevance_note: First-party chronology and September 10 investigation statement concerning whether Buckmaster's recent Codex prompts could have influenced the Navier–Stokes system.
baseline_sources.source_context: OpenAI states that the effort began after hearing a rumor later linked to Alpöge and Buckmaster, used a large multi-agent system, and that its researchers and agents did not see their work before public release. A 10 September update says that, following an internal investigation, Buckmaster's Codex prompts over the preceding two months could not have influenced the system in any way, including through training.
baseline_sources.system_or_product: internal OpenAI research model, Codex and GPT-6 Astra
baseline_sources.model_or_algorithm: internal unreleased model; GPT-6 Astra used for Lean formalization and verification
